givtcp_entities_missing.title: GivTCP entities not found
givtcp_entities_missing.description:
One or more GivTCP sensor entities configured during setup are no longer registered in Home Assistant. This usually means GivTCP was reinstalled with a different inverter serial, or the entity IDs changed.

To fix: go to **Settings → Integrations → GivEnergy Inverter Manager → Configure** and run the reconfiguration wizard to re-select the correct entities.

min_soc_too_high.title: Battery minimum SoC is set too high
min_soc_too_high.description:
**Battery minimum SoC** is currently {min_soc}%. On nights when charging is skipped, the integration writes this value as the inverter's charge target. A value this high causes the inverter to hold the battery at {min_soc}% all night, importing from the grid instead of discharging.

Recommended value: 10–20%. Go to **Settings → Integrations → GivEnergy Inverter Manager → Configure → Battery** and lower Battery minimum SoC.

confirm.title: Clear the other charge slots
confirm.description:
The integration manages charge slot 1 only. These other slots also have a charge window: {slots}.

The inverter charges in every active slot, so a leftover slot can charge the battery at a dearer rate than the cheapest period.

Selecting **Submit** sets the start and end time of each of them to 00:00. Slot 1 is not changed. You can also clear them yourself in GivTCP.

abort.dry_run: Dry run is on, so nothing was changed. Turn it off in the integration options to clear the slots.
abort.write_failed: GivTCP did not accept every write. The slots that are still active stay listed. Check that GivTCP is running, then try again.
abort.not_loaded: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not loaded. Reload it, then try again.

config_entry_not_ready.message: First data fetch failed. Check that GivTCP is running and MQTT is connected. ({error})

givtcp_unavailable.message: GivTCP is not publishing data — solar and battery sensors are unavailable. Check that GivTCP is running and MQTT is connected.

no_config_entry.message: GivEnergy Inverter Manager is not configured. Add the integration in Settings → Integrations before calling this service.

dashboard_write_failed.message: Failed to write dashboard file to the Home Assistant config directory. Check that HA has write access to the config folder.

get_dashboard_yaml.name: Get dashboard YAML
get_dashboard_yaml.description: Writes a Lovelace dashboard pre-filled with your actual entity IDs to givenergy_dashboard.yaml in the Home Assistant config directory, then shows a persistent notification with setup steps. Paste the file into a new blank dashboard via Raw configuration editor, or point a YAML-mode dashboard at it.

suggest_appliance_run.name: Suggest appliance run time
suggest_appliance_run.description: Checks whether now is a good time to run a high-load appliance (washing machine, dishwasher, etc.) based on current solar surplus, battery state, and the active tariff rate. Creates a persistent notification with the verdict and the reason. The action does not return a response.

appliance_name.name: Appliance name
appliance_name.description: Name of the appliance (used in the notification)

appliance_power_w.name: Appliance power (W)
appliance_power_w.description: Rated power consumption of the appliance in watts

get_roi_summary.name: Get ROI summary
get_roi_summary.description: Returns return-on-investment figures for today, this week, this month and this year, plus battery cycles and remaining life. Use response_variable to read the result in a script or automation. Returns an empty response until the first update has completed.

compare_tariff.name: Compare tariff
compare_tariff.description: Compares this bill period against a flat-rate alternative tariff, using the kWh imported and exported so far this period. Both tariffs are billed the same way: energy, supplier saving, standing charge, PSO levy, VAT, then the export credit. The alternative uses your tariff's supplier discount, VAT and PSO levy unless you enter your own. With more than one entry set up, the response lists every entry. Use response_variable to read the result.

rate.name: Import rate
rate.description: Flat import rate of the alternative tariff, per kWh

standing_charge.name: Standing charge per day
standing_charge.description: Daily standing charge of the alternative tariff

export_rate.name: Export rate
export_rate.description: Export rate of the alternative tariff, per kWh

discount_rate.name: Supplier discount
discount_rate.description: Supplier discount of the alternative tariff in percent. Leave empty to use your tariff's discount

vat_rate.name: VAT rate
vat_rate.description: VAT of the alternative tariff in percent. Leave empty to use your tariff's VAT rate

pso_levy.name: PSO levy
pso_levy.description: PSO levy of the alternative tariff for a whole bill period. Leave empty to use your tariff's PSO levy

year_on_year_summary.name: Year-on-year summary
year_on_year_summary.description: Compares this bill period with the same period one year ago. The comparison needs 12 completed bill periods. Until then the response has no_data set to true and shows how many periods are stored. Use response_variable to read the result.

export_energy_data.name: Export energy data
export_energy_data.description: Writes today, yesterday, this week, this month, this year and each stored completed bill period to givenergy_energy_export.csv in the Home Assistant config directory, then shows a persistent notification. The action does not return a response.
